title_en: US has floated Ukraine ceding Donbas for Nato membership, Zelensky says
title_zh: 泽伦斯基表示，美国已提议乌克兰放弃顿巴斯以加入北约
summary: The US has not confirmed the Ukrainian president's comments - a US official told the BBC "many ideas continue to be discussed".
summary_zh: 美国尚未证实乌克兰总统的言论——一位美国官员告诉英国广播公司“许多想法仍在讨论中”。
body_en: By Aleks Phillips and Sarah Rainsford , Southern and Eastern Europe correspondent , Reporting from Kyiv
US negotiators have touted the idea of Ukraine withdrawing its remaining forces from the eastern Donbas region in exchange for Nato membership, President Volodymyr Zelensky has said.
The US has not confirmed Zelensky's comments, and a US official told the BBC "many ideas continue to be discussed but any final deal will have to be agreed to by both parties".
The Ukrainian leader's comments came after US envoys met Russian President Vladimir Putin and Zelensky as part of US efforts to end the war between Russia and Ukraine.
Kyiv has long sought membership of the military alliance, but this has previously been opposed by the US and others while Russia has said another Nato member on its border is unacceptable.

Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. It controls most of the industrial region of Donbas and Zelensky has consistently said Ukraine is unwilling to give up sovereign territory.

"The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?' This was the first time this had been raised," Zelensky said in remarks released by his office on Saturday.
He went on to say that if he received a specific proposal that contained security guarantees, no constraints on Ukraine's military and funds to rebuild the country, he would put it to a referendum.
US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff travelled to the Irish capital, Dublin, on Thursday to meet Zelensky, after a round of talks with Putin in Moscow.

Comments by both Putin and Kremlin officials suggest that Russia's position on the war has not shifted. It has previously proposed limits on the size of Ukraine's military, territorial concessions and Kyiv's guaranteed neutrality as conditions of a peace deal.
Ukraine has rejected these, arguing that such constraints would hamper its ability to stave off any future invasion.
Other Nato members apart from the US are wary of membership for Ukraine - and it is understood that Ukraine itself sees that as unrealistic.
The Kremlin has always been fiercely opposed, too. It is one reason why Russia started this war in the first place.

It is possible the American envoys were exploring Ukraine's "red lines" when it comes to occupied land in the Donbas. Zelensky said recently that the US mediators believed Kyiv only had to cede territory to achieve peace and were applying pressure, keen to do a deal as soon as possible.
Ukraine is sure that Russia's ambitions are far greater and has long seen Nato as its only sure protection.
So it is also possible that Zelensky made this suggestion public in order to re-open a discussion that had been considered all-but closed.
He maintains that the idea is now "back on the agenda" as part of an "extremely difficult conversation" on European security.
It also looks like Ukrainian push-back against Russia's renewed hardline stance. Moscow now talks about a "new European security architecture", which is long-standing Russian code for a weaker Nato.
The issue appears to have been the main focus at the latest round of talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi this week.
Hours after Zelensky's remarks, Jared Kushner appeared keen to dampen down any US offer of Nato membership for Ukraine, urging "confidentiality" in a sensitive process.
body_zh: 作者：Aleks Phillips 和 Sarah Rainsford，南欧和东欧记者，基辅报道
总统泽连斯基表示，美国谈判代表提出了乌克兰从顿巴斯东部地区撤出剩余部队以换取北约成员资格的想法。
美国尚未证实泽伦斯基的言论，一名美国官员告诉英国广播公司“许多想法仍在讨论，但任何最终协议都必须得到双方同意”。
这位乌克兰领导人发表上述言论之前，美国特使会见了俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和泽连斯基，这是美国结束俄罗斯和乌克兰之间战争努力的一部分。
基辅长期以来一直寻求加入军事联盟，但此前曾遭到美国和其他国家的反对，而俄罗斯则表示其边境的另一个北约成员国是不可接受的。
俄罗斯于2022年2月对乌克兰发动全面入侵，控制着顿巴斯大部分工业区，泽连斯基一直表示乌克兰不愿放弃主权领土。
“美国人提出了一个问题：‘如果乌克兰加入北约怎么办？乌克兰会从顿巴斯撤军吗？’这是第一次提出这个问题，”泽连斯基在其办公室周六发表的讲话中表示。
他接着说，如果他收到一项包含安全保障、对乌克兰军事和重建国家资金不施加限制的具体提案，他将把它付诸公投。
在莫斯科与普京进行一轮会谈后，美国特使贾里德·库什纳和史蒂夫·威特科夫周四前往爱尔兰首都都柏林会见泽连斯基。
普京和克里姆林宫官员的评论表明，俄罗斯对战争的立场没有改变。此前，它曾提议限制乌克兰的军事规模、领土让步以及基辅保证中立，作为和平协议的条件。
乌克兰拒绝了这些限制，认为此类限制将削弱其抵御未来入侵的能力。
除美国之外的其他北约成员国对乌克兰的加入持谨慎态度 - 据了解，乌克兰本身也认为这是不现实的。
克里姆林宫也一直强烈反对。这是俄罗斯首先发动这场战争的原因之一。
美国特使可能正在探索乌克兰在顿巴斯被占领土地上的“红线”。泽连斯基最近表示，美国调解人认为基辅只需割让领土即可实现和平，并正在施加压力，渴望尽快达成协议。
乌克兰确信俄罗斯的野心要大得多，并且长期以来一直将北约视为其唯一可靠的保护。
因此，泽连斯基公开这一建议也有可能是为了重新开启一场原本被认为几乎已经结束的讨论。
他坚称，这个想法现在“重新提上议程”，作为欧洲安全“极其困难的对话”的一部分。
这看起来也像是乌克兰对俄罗斯重新采取强硬立场的反击。莫斯科现在谈论的是“新的欧洲安全架构”，这是俄罗斯长期以来对北约实力较弱的代言。
这个问题似乎是乌克兰、俄罗斯和美国本周在阿布扎比举行的最新一轮会谈的主要焦点。
泽连斯基发表讲话数小时后，贾里德·库什纳似乎热衷于抑制美国向乌克兰提出加入北约的提议，并敦促在敏感过程中“保密”。

title_en: Netanyahu says only a unity government can guarantee Israel’s security
title_zh: 内塔尼亚胡表示只有联合政府才能保证以色列的安全
summary: Eisenkot, in charge of forming a government, dismisses the appeal as ‘tricks’ as talks and a Knesset speaker vote loom.
summary_zh: 负责组建政府的艾森科特驳斥了这一呼吁，称其为“诡计”，因为谈判和议会发言人投票即将到来。
body_en: Share Netanyahu says only a unity government can guarantee Israel’s security on social media
Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has renewed his call for a national unity government with his rival, Gadi Eisenkot, saying only such a government can guarantee Israel’s security.
In a video statement on Saturday, Netanyahu said a meeting with Eisenkot on Thursday “only strengthened the conviction that it is essential to form a national unity government”.

The prime minister said such a government could “eliminate the Iranian threat once and for all”, claiming Tehran would “not hesitate to use nuclear weapons against us”.
“Let’s meet in one room, without preconditions,” he said.
Within minutes, however, Eisenkot dismissed the appeal as a ploy.
A former army chief, Eisenkot said Netanyahu “knows he lost the election”.
“Netanyahu is calling for negotiations while they are already underway,” he said. “These tricks don’t work on me.”

Neither side won a majority in the October 27 election. Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc took 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, Eisenkot’s four-party bloc got 48 seats, and Arab-led parties won a record 19.
President Isaac Herzog last week tasked Eisenkot with forming a government, after 67 lawmakers, including those from Arab-led parties, endorsed him, while 46 backed Netanyahu.
Eisenkot has 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension. He has ruled out including Arab-led parties in his government.

Under Eisenkot’s plan for a minority “national emergency government”, his bloc’s 48 lawmakers would vote in favour against the 46 Netanyahu supporters, while the 26 lawmakers from Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties could abstain. It would allow his government to be approved without an absolute majority in the Knesset.
Netanyahu has warned that such a government would lead to Israel’s “collapse”.

Netanyahu’s version would include Jewish parties from the centre and the right and exclude Arab parties . He and his allies have made unsubstantiated claims that Arab-led parties “stole” the election.
On Friday, Eisenkot called Netanyahu’s campaign against them “racist” .

Eisenkot has said he could work with members of Netanyahu’s Likud party and with Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionism if their commitment to unity is “sincere”, but he insisted on a “break with the extremists”, notably supporters of far-right minister Itamar Ben-Gvir.
The Knesset will elect its speaker on Tuesday. The post is currently held by Netanyahu ally Amir Ohana, and the opposition has put forward Matan Kahana, a former military officer, in his place.
body_zh: 内塔尼亚胡表示，只有联合政府才能保证以色列在社交媒体上的安全
以色列看守总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡再次呼吁与其竞争对手加迪·艾森科特组建民族团结政府，并表示只有这样的政府才能保证以色列的安全。
内塔尼亚胡在周六的视频声明中表示，周四与艾森科特的会面“更加坚定了组建民族团结政府的必要性”。

总理表示，这样的政府可以“一劳永逸地消除伊朗的威胁”，并声称德黑兰将“毫不犹豫地对我们使用核武器”。
“让我们在一个房间里见面，没有先决条件，”他说。
然而几分钟之内，艾森科特就驳回了上诉，认为这是一种策略。
艾森科特曾担任陆军参谋长，他表示内塔尼亚胡“知道他输掉了选举”。
“内塔尼亚胡呼吁谈判已经在进行中，”他说。 “这些伎俩对我不起作用。”
在 10 月 27 日的选举中，双方都没有赢得多数席位。内塔尼亚胡的右翼和宗教集团在议会 120 个席位中占据了 53 个席位，艾森科特的四党集团获得了 48 个席位，阿拉伯领导的政党赢得了创纪录的 19 个席位。
总统艾萨克·赫尔佐格上周责成艾森科特组建政府，此前有 67 名议员（包括阿拉伯领导政党的议员）支持他，而 46 名议员支持内塔尼亚胡。
Eisenkot 有 28 天，可能还可以延长 14 天。他排除了将阿拉伯领导的政党纳入其政府的可能性。
根据艾森科特的少数派“国家紧急政府”计划，其集团的48名议员将投票赞成反对46名内塔尼亚胡支持者，而来自阿拉伯和极端正统政党的26名议员则可以弃权。这将使他的政府无需在议会中获得绝对多数就能获得批准。
内塔尼亚胡警告说，这样的政府将导致以色列“崩溃”。
内塔尼亚胡的版本将包括中间派和右翼的犹太政党，并排除阿拉伯政党。他和他的盟友毫无根据地声称阿拉伯领导的政党“窃取”了选举。
周五，艾森科特称内塔尼亚胡针对他们的竞选活动是“种族主义”。
艾森科特表示，如果内塔尼亚胡领导的利库德集团成员以及比扎莱尔·斯莫特里奇领导的宗教犹太复国主义对团结的承诺“真诚”，他可以与他们合作，但他坚持“与极端分子决裂”，特别是极右翼部长伊塔马尔·本-格维尔的支持者。
议会将于周二选举议长。该职位目前由内塔尼亚胡盟友阿米尔·奥哈纳担任，反对派已提名前军官马坦·卡哈纳接替他的职位。

title_en: US envoy Kushner says he aims to broker Europe-Russia talks on Ukraine
title_zh: 美国特使库什纳表示，他的目标是促成欧洲与俄罗斯就乌克兰问题进行谈判
summary: Europe's direct engagement with Moscow as part of Ukraine-Russia peace talks is edging closer to becoming a reality.
summary_zh: 作为乌克兰-俄罗斯和平谈判的一部分，欧洲与莫斯科的直接接触正在接近成为现实。
body_en: US envoy Kushner says he aims to broker Europe-Russia talks on Ukraine | News | Al Jazeera

US envoy Jared Kushner has said he is working with Russia, Ukraine and Europe to move peace talks to the next stage, including facilitating direct engagement between Europe and Moscow.
Kushner told reporters Saturday that “both sides” know that compromises will be necessary to end the war, and that he and fellow envoy Steve Witkoff were now working on next steps.

Trump son-in-law’s comments follow peace talks in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday that failed to reach a breakthrough on ending the war, but resulted in a prisoner exchange .

The prospect of Europe’s involvement in the talks has grown in recent weeks, with leaders agreeing on Friday to send five representatives of European countries to represent the bloc at future peace talks.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Wednesday he did not think it was possible to think about European security “without Europe”.
The Kremlin has signalled an openness to negotiations with Europe, but it has criticised a lack of proposals from the bloc.

The five countries attending are the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Italy, and Poland – the five countries that have signalled readiness to send troops as part of a “coalition of the willing” to secure Ukraine in the event of a ceasefire.
In a lengthy post on X on Saturday, French President Emmanuel Macron said that the bloc must “state clearly” what it wants for the post-war period, “including to the Russians”.

Macron also stated his belief that Ukraine, which has Europe’s largest conventional army, has a key role to play in Europe’s post-war context alongside NATO, which he added is a “place where it fully belongs”.
Zelenskyy said Friday that US negotiators had asked during the Abu Dhabi talks whether Ukraine would withdraw its troops from its eastern region of Donbas in exchange for joining NATO.
The war has raged while negotiations continue. November leaks from Russia’s official statistics agency showed that Russia’s war effort has so far cost the lives of at least 450,000 soldiers.

title_en: Sotheby's auction of $180m Van Gogh challenged over claims it was 'sold under duress'
title_zh: 苏富比拍卖行价值 1.8 亿美元的梵高作品因声称其“在胁迫下出售”而受到质疑
summary: Sotheby's says it will work with the heirs of a family who had previously owned the artwork to try and reach a solution.
summary_zh: 苏富比表示，将与曾拥有该艺术品的家族继承人合作，尝试达成解决方案。
body_en: Auction house Sotheby's says it is working to resolve a dispute over the intended sale of a painting by Vincent van Gogh.
Châtaigniers en Fleurs, which carries an estimate of $180m (£136m), is due to go under the hammer in New York on Wednesday.
But representatives acting for heirs of the Fischer family - earlier German owners of the work - say it may have been sold under duress during the rise of the Nazis.
Sotheby's say its own "extensive research" has not established this, but say they will work with the family to try and reach a solution.

"Sotheby's takes provenance and restitution matters extremely seriously and has undertaken extensive research into the ownership history of Châtaigniers en fleurs," Sotheby's told the BBC in a statement.
"We are aware of the concerns recently raised by representatives of the Fischer heirs and have been in dialogue with them regarding the painting's history.

"While our research to date has not established that the painting was sold under duress, we recognize the importance of engaging thoughtfully and constructively with the family and are committed to working toward a mutually satisfactory resolution."
The painting - whose name translates as Blossoming Chestnut Trees - is being sold as part of a set called the Blaquier-Arrieta Collection.
Sotheby's website details the provenance of the oil painting and how it has researched the artwork changing hands since 1890.
It says Samuel Fischer - a famous German publisher - acquired it 1909 before it was passed down in his family after his death in 1934.
The painting was deposited with Paul Cassirer in Amsterdam in 1932 or 1933 before it went to Henriette and Marcel Kapferer in Paris in 1936, Sotherby's says.
Four other owners have had it since before it was put up for auction this year.
Fischer family heirs have instructed a lawyer who, according to the New York Times , external , has written to Sotherby's.
He is said to have told the auction house the painting was sold in Amsterdam before World War Two because of financial losses the Fischer family's publishing company suffered under the Nazis.
The BBC has contacted the lawyer for comment.
body_zh: 拍卖行苏富比表示，正在努力解决有关文森特·梵高画作拟出售的争议。
Châtaigniers en Fleurs 的估价为 1.8 亿美元（1.36 亿英镑），定于周三在纽约进行拍卖。
但代表费舍尔家族继承人（该作品的早期德国所有者）的代表表示，该作品可能是在纳粹崛起期间被迫出售的。
苏富比表示，其自己的“广泛研究”尚未证实这一点，但表示他们将与家人合作，尝试达成解决方案。
苏富比在一份声明中告诉英国广播公司：“苏富比非常重视出处和归还问题，并对 Châtaigniers en fleurs 的所有权历史进行了广泛的研究。”
“我们意识到费舍尔继承人代表最近提出的担忧，并一直在与他们就这幅画的历史进行对话。
“虽然我们迄今为止的研究尚未证实这幅画是在胁迫下出售的，但我们认识到与家人进行深思熟虑和建设性接触的重要性，并致力于达成双方都满意的解决方案。”
这幅画的名字翻译为“开花的栗子树”，作为 Blaquier-Arrieta 系列的一部分出售。
苏富比网站详细介绍了这幅油画的出处，以及自 1890 年以来它如何研究这件艺术品的转手情况。
据称，德国著名出版商塞缪尔·费舍尔 (Samuel Fischer) 于 1909 年购买了这本书，1934 年塞缪尔·费舍尔去世后，该书由其家族传承。
苏瑟比拍卖行称，这幅画于 1932 年或 1933 年存放在阿姆斯特丹的保罗·卡西尔 (Paul Cassirer) 手中，随后于 1936 年被巴黎的亨利埃特·卡普费雷尔 (Henriette Kapferer) 和马塞尔·卡普费雷尔 (Marcel Kapferer) 收藏。
在今年它被拍卖之前，其他四位所有者就已经拥有它。
据《纽约时报》外部报道，费舍尔家族的继承人已委托一名律师致函苏瑟比拍卖行。
据说他告诉拍卖行，这幅画是在第二次世界大战前在阿姆斯特丹出售的，因为费舍尔家族的出版公司在纳粹统治下遭受了经济损失。
BBC 已联系该律师征求意见。

title_en: COP31: Protesters, UN urge swift climate deal
title_zh: COP31：抗议者、联合国敦促迅速达成气候协议
summary: The UN climate chief has warned that "tactical delays" at the COP31 climate talks in Turkey could prevent a deal to slow global warming.
summary_zh: 联合国气候负责人警告说，在土耳其举行的第 31 届联合国气候变化框架公约 (COP31) 气候谈判上的“战术性拖延”可能会阻碍达成减缓全球变暖的协议。
body_en: The United Nations' top climate official urged negotiators at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey to "avoid tactical delays" that would prevent a deal to stop global warming.
Delegates from more than 200 nations are gathered in the Mediterranean city of Antalya with the core goal of preventing the planet from warming by 2 degrees Celsius (3.6 degrees Fahrenheit).
Downtown, thousands of civil society and environmental activists from around the world protested against the consequences of climate change .
COP31: Can electrification replace fossil fuels?
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Simon Stiell, executive secretary of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), said getting an agreement is "tough but vital work."
"There ​is no collective success without compromise from every party," he added.
"As we head into the second week, ​I urge ‌parties to move swiftly to the hardest issues and to avoid tactical delays."
Climate protest draws activists from around the world
Meanwhile, tens of thousands of protesters marched through Antalya on Saturday for climate protection and human rights, according to organizers.
Many were dismayed at the lack of progress and how the climate crisis is taking a back seat.

"The pursuit of profit at all costs continues to set the [global] agenda [and] govern the trajectory of our world, so there is a need to push back," environmental activist Zaki Mamdoo from South Africa told DW.
Luisa Nebauer, the main organizer of Germany's Fridays for Future movement, lamented that German Chancellor Friedrich Merz was absent from the conference, along with several other European leaders.
"We won't have a chance to solve any of the crises as long as our planet is destabilizing by the hour," Nebauer told DW. "We must show up!"
Turkish authorities permitted the rally to go ahead, in a country that often bans large public gatherings.
Alongside the march, a parallel "People's Climate Summit" involving hundreds of domestic and international civil society groups takes place in Antalya this weekend.
As Turkey hosts COP31 its beaches are becoming too hot for sea turtles

With inflation, wars, deindustrialization and debt being seen as bigger immediate threats, many governments are watering down their commitments to the clean energy transition, along with the billions required to help developing nations to adapt.
The United ⁠States has snubbed the talks ​for the second year in a row under President Donald Trump, who has called climate change a hoax and promoted continued use of fossil fuels.
body_zh: 联合国气候变化高级官员敦促在土耳其举行的第三十一届缔约方会议气候峰会上的谈判代表“避免战术上的拖延”，否则将阻止达成阻止全球变暖的协议。
来自 200 多个国家的代表齐聚地中海城市安塔利亚，其核心目标是防止地球变暖 2 摄氏度（3.6 华氏度）。
在市中心，来自世界各地的数千名民间社会和环保活动人士抗议气候变化的后果。
COP31：电气化能否取代化石燃料？
要观看此视频，请启用 JavaScript，并考虑升级到支持 HTML5 视频的网络浏览器
联合国气候变化框架公约（UNFCCC）执行秘书西蒙·斯蒂尔表示，达成协议是“艰巨但至关重要的工作”。
“没有各方的妥协，就不会有集体的成功，”他补充道。
“当我们进入第二周时，我敦促各方迅速采取行动解决最棘手的问题，避免战术上的拖延。”
气候抗议吸引了来自世界各地的活动人士
与此同时，据组织者称，周六，数万名抗议者在安塔利亚游行，呼吁保护气候和人权。
许多人对缺乏进展以及气候危机如何退居二线感到沮丧。
来自南非的环保活动家扎基·马姆杜 (Zaki Mamdoo) 告诉德国之声：“不惜一切代价追求利润继续制定[全球]议程[并]控制我们世界的发展轨迹，因此有必要予以抵制。”
德国“星期五为未来”运动的主要组织者路易莎·内鲍尔对德国总理弗里德里希·梅尔茨以及其他几位欧洲领导人缺席会议表示遗憾。
内鲍尔告诉德国之声：“只要我们的星球每时每刻都在不稳定，我们就没有机会解决任何危机。” “我们必须出现！”
土耳其当局允许集会继续进行，因为该国经常禁止大型公众集会。
在游行的同时，本周末在安塔利亚举行了一场平行的“人民气候峰会”，数百个国内和国际民间社会团体参加。
随着土耳其主办 COP31，其海滩对于海龟来说变得太热
由于通货膨胀、战争、去工业化和债务被视为更大的直接威胁，许多政府正在淡化其对清洁能源转型的承诺，以及帮助发展中国家适应所需的数十亿美元的承诺。
在唐纳德·特朗普总统的领导下，美国连续第二年冷落此次会谈，特朗普称气候变化是一个骗局，并提倡继续使用化石燃料。

title_en: Choking fires, deadly heat and devastating floods: 2026 in extreme weather
title_zh: 令人窒息的大火、致命的高温和毁灭性的洪水：2026 年的极端天气
summary: People around the world have contended with unprecedented weather events and their fatal effects caused by the climate catastrophe After the world’s hottest summer since records began in 1850, the death toll from extreme weather in 2026 is already in the high
summary_zh: 世界各地的人们一直在应对前所未有的天气事件及其由气候灾难造成的致命影响。
body_en: People around the world have contended with unprecedented weather events and their fatal effects caused by the climate catastrophe

A fter the world’s hottest summer since records began in 1850, the death toll from extreme weather in 2026 is already in the high tens of thousands. That is a conservative estimate and is certain to rise much higher.

As Cop31 continues and scientists warn that climate breakdown may be accelerating , the Guardian looks back at a year of droughts, fires and floods as a reminder that, unless the world takes urgent action to cut emissions, this disastrous year will be one of the best of the rest of our lives.
Chart showing how the past four years have overturned all monthly temperature records J anuary

As temperatures jump nearly 20C (68F) above average , Victoria and other southern states register new heat records, including 50C in Port Augusta and the tiny opal mining town of Andamooka. Melbourne hospitals report a 25% increase in heat-related illnesses, while authorities in many areas struggle with wildfires. Scientists say the supercharged climate has made the heatwave five times more likely. Heatwaves already cause more deaths in Australia than all other natural hazards combined.
Mudslides kill 72 in Brazil after record rain

The city of Juiz de Fora in Minas Gerais records its wettest ever month , triggering landslides that sweep away hundreds of homes in poor communities on unstable hillsides. Floods also disrupt Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo. More than 10,000 people are displaced.

In Ethiopia, at least 131 people are killed in floods and mudslides that bury entire villages. Eighty die in Kenya and 18 in Tanzania. The Arabian peninsula is battered by fierce winds and heavy downpours that flood the streets of the desert kingdom. Hailstones the size of tennis balls fall in Oman and lightning storms leave cities in the UAE inundated with water . Many areas report record rainfall. At least 30 die in Afghanistan as heavy rains trigger landslides. Hong Kong is soaked in twice the usual monthly precipitation. Flood waters in southern Russia submerge homes and leave more than 300,000 without electricity. Huge tracts of farmland are left underwater in Argentina and Chile.

The World Meteorological Organization reveals an alarming buildup of energy in Earth’s system. More than 90% is stored in the oceans, where warming has more than doubled over the past two decades compared with the average over the previous 45 years. This makes weather more extreme and threatens health and food supplies. António Guterres, the UN secretary general, says: “The global climate is in a state of emergency. Planet Earth is being pushed beyond its limits. Every key climate indicator is flashing red.” Guterres urges the world to cut fossil fuel emissions as rapidly as possible to minimise future risks. However, CO 2 in the atmosphere continues to rise.
Graph showing atmospheric CO2 concentration A pril
Super typhoon tears through Micronesia, Guam and Saipan

At peak intensity on 12 April, Sinlaku registers a wind speed of 295km/h (183mph) – roughly the same as a Shinkansen bullet train and the joint highest recorded by a storm in the western Pacific basin so early in the year. It is also the deadliest in decades, killing 12 , leaving 43,000 without power, forcing mass evacuation and causing $1.5bn (£1.1bn) in damages. This will remain one of the most powerful storms of 2026, superseded only by Super Typhoon Champi that will strike Taiwan and Japan in October.
Hundreds of millions endure deadly heat in south Asia

At least 47 heat-related deaths are reported in southern Asia as temperatures soar above 45C in several Indian and Bangladeshi cities, and hit a peak of 52C in Pakistan’s southern province of Sindh. Scientists warn that the climate crisis is exposing hundreds of millions of people in south Asia to longer, deadlier pre-monsoon heat .

Sea surface temperature graphs begin to jag upwards and away from all previous highs on 21 June, starting a trend that will worsen over the rest of the year. This alarms scientists because oceans absorb more than 90% of the excess energy in Earth’s system. If the seas start to release that heat then the land and air will get warmer more quickly. This coincides with the emergence of the latest El Niño , which is confirmed on 2 June.
Arctic and Antarctic swelter in unprecedented warmth

Instead of the usual winter snow and ice, scientists at the Esperanza base on the Trinity peninsula of Antarctica are astonished to see rain and dirt outside their windows after an eight-day heatwave that peaked with a record temperature of 15C on 6 June. At the other end of the planet, the Arctic experiences its warmest ever June . Beliy Island, Siberia, registers 28.3C on 25 June, the highest temperature ever recorded that far north in the Eurasian Arctic.

Relentless rains claim almost 100 lives in west Africa from May to June. Record downpours of up to 140mm (5.5in) in a single day are made five times more likely and 23% more intense by the human-caused climate crisis. Floods and mudslides kill 59 in Côte d’Ivoire, 35 in Ghana and five in Togo .

Almost 1,000 wildfires sweep across Canada, charring 3m hectares (7.4m acres) and sending a haze of smoke as far as New York. On 15 July Toronto registers the world’s worst air quality as a result of the haze. Smoke kills 4,000 people in Canada each year , almost four times as many as at the start of the century. Meanwhile, in Europe, prolonged droughts create tinderbox conditions for wildfires in Greece, Portugal, Italy, Norway, Germany, Spain and France. They burn 686,000 hectares in Europe, twice the average of the past 20 years .
body_zh: 世界各地的人们都在应对前所未有的天气事件及其由气候灾难造成的致命影响
在经历了自 1850 年有记录以来世界上最热的夏季之后，2026 年极端天气造成的死亡人数已高达数万人。这是一个保守的估计，并且肯定会上涨得更高。
随着第三十一届缔约方会议的继续进行，科学家警告气候崩溃可能正在加速，《卫报》回顾了干旱、火灾和洪水的一年，提醒我们，除非世界采取紧急行动减少排放，否则这一灾难性的一年将是我们余生中最美好的一年。
图表显示过去四年如何推翻所有月度气温记录
随着气温比平均水平高出近 20 摄氏度（68 华氏度），维多利亚州和其他南部各州创下了新的高温记录，其中包括奥古斯塔港的 50 摄氏度和蛋白石开采小镇安达穆卡。墨尔本医院报告称，与高温相关的疾病增加了 25%，而许多地区的当局正在努力应对野火。科学家表示，过度的气候使热浪发生的可能性增加了五倍。热浪在澳大利亚造成的死亡人数已经超过了所有其他自然灾害的总和。
巴西创纪录降雨后泥石流造成72人死亡
米纳斯吉拉斯州的茹伊斯德福拉市迎来了有史以来最潮湿的一个月，引发山体滑坡，摧毁了不稳定山坡上贫困社区的数百所房屋。洪水还扰乱了里约热内卢和圣保罗。超过10,000人流离失所。

在埃塞俄比亚，洪水和泥石流掩埋了整个村庄，造成至少 131 人死亡。肯尼亚有 80 人死亡，坦桑尼亚有 18 人死亡。阿拉伯半岛遭受狂风和倾盆大雨的袭击，淹没了这个沙漠王国的街道。网球大小的冰雹落在阿曼，雷暴使阿联酋的城市被水淹没。许多地区报告降雨量创历史新高。阿富汗暴雨引发山体滑坡，造成至少 30 人死亡。香港每月的降水量是平常的两倍。俄罗斯南部的洪水淹没了房屋，导致超过 30 万居民断电。阿根廷和智利的大片农田被淹没在水下。
世界气象组织揭示了地球系统中能量的惊人积累。超过 90% 储存在海洋中，过去 20 年来海洋变暖程度是过去 45 年平均水平的两倍多。这使得天气变得更加极端，并威胁健康和粮食供应。联合国秘书长安东尼奥·古特雷斯表示：“全球气候正处于紧急状态。地球正在超出其极限。每一个关键的气候指标都在闪烁红色。”古特雷斯敦促世界尽快减少化石燃料排放，以尽量减少未来的风险。然而，大气中的CO 2 持续上升。
显示四月大气二氧化碳浓度的图表
超强台风席卷密克罗尼西亚、关岛和塞班岛
4 月 12 日，辛拉库的峰值强度达到 295 公里/小时（183 英里/小时），与新干线子弹头列车的风速大致相同，也是今年早些时候西太平洋盆地风暴记录的最高风速。这也是几十年来最严重的一次，造成 12 人死亡，43,000 人断电，迫使大规模疏散，并造成 15 亿美元（11 亿英镑）的损失。这仍将是 2026 年最强大的风暴之一，仅次于 10 月份袭击台湾和日本的超级台风“占比”。
南亚数亿人忍受致命高温
据报道，南亚地区至少有 47 人因高温死亡，印度和孟加拉国几个城市的气温飙升至 45 摄氏度以上，巴基斯坦南部信德省的最高气温达到 52 摄氏度。科学家警告说，气候危机使南亚数亿人面临季风前更长时间、更致命的高温。
6 月 21 日，海面温度图表开始急剧上升，远离之前的所有高点，开始出现一种在今年剩余时间里恶化的趋势。这让科学家们感到震惊，因为海洋吸收了地球系统 90% 以上的多余能量。如果海洋开始释放热量，那么陆地和空气就会更快变暖。这恰逢最近一次厄尔尼诺现象的出现，并于 6 月 2 日得到证实。
北极和南极地区前所未有的酷热
南极洲三一半岛埃斯佩兰萨基地的科学家们惊讶地发现，在经历了为期八天的热浪之后，他们的窗外不再是平常的冬季冰雪，6月6日的最高气温达到创纪录的15摄氏度。在地球的另一端，北极正经历有史以来最温暖的六月。 6 月 25 日，西伯利亚贝利岛的气温达到 28.3 摄氏度，这是欧亚北极地区有记录以来的最高气温。
5 月至 6 月，西非连续不断的降雨夺去了近 100 人的生命。由于人为造成的气候危机，单日降雨量达到创纪录的 140 毫米（5.5 英寸）的倾盆大雨的可能性增加了五倍，强度增加了 23%。洪水和泥石流导致科特迪瓦 59 人死亡、加纳 35 人死亡、多哥 5 人死亡。

近 1,000 场野火席卷了加拿大各地，烧焦了 300 万公顷（740 万英亩）土地，浓烟甚至蔓延至纽约。 7 月 15 日，多伦多因雾霾而出现世界上最差的空气质量。加拿大每年有 4,000 人因烟雾死亡，几乎是本世纪初的四倍。与此同时，在欧洲，长期干旱为希腊、葡萄牙、意大利、挪威、德国、西班牙和法国的野火创造了易燃易爆的条件。欧洲烧毁面积达 686,000 公顷，是过去 20 年平均面积的两倍。

title_en: Hungarian authorities uncover $20m during probe of Orbán-era minister
title_zh: 匈牙利当局在对欧尔班时代部长的调查中发现 2000 万美元
summary: Prime Minister Péter Magyar promised a sweeping anti-corruption drive after ousting Orbán in April.
summary_zh: 总理彼得·马扎尔 (Péter Magyar) 在四月份罢免欧尔班后承诺开展全面反腐败行动。
body_en: Image source, The National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (NVVH)
Nearly $20m (£14.8m) in cash has been found hidden in farm buildings and buried in forests as part of an investigation into a former minister of Viktor Orbán, authorities have said.

Miklós Seszták, who served as minister of national development for four of the ex-prime minister's 16-year rule, is accused of accepting bribes as part of a scheme involving the state transport company. He has denied any wrongdoing.
Hungary's new Prime Minister Péter Magyar unseated Orbán in a landslide election in April on the promise of launching a sweeping anti-corruption drive.
On Friday, following the two-day search for the cash - found in secluded locations across the country - Magyar described it as the end of the "mafia".

Investigators found wads of banknotes in safes, buried in woodlands and hidden in agricultural and residential buildings and warehouses, as part of the probe into Seszták, the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (NVVH) said in a statement.
The cash amounted to "5,071,632,000 forints, €2,658,350 and $1,257,100", it added, bringing the combined value to $19.5m. It has been deposited into the Hungarian State Treasury, the body said.
The NVVH was established to investigate allegations of corruption during the Orbán rule, which Magyar has dubbed "Operation Purgatory".
Magyar promised Hungarians "regime change" during the election earlier this year and has set about undoing many Orbán-era policies since entering office.
Allegations of corruption and cronyism have long dogged Orbán, who during the course of his tenure turned Hungary into what the EU characterised as an "electoral autocracy".
His government faced accusations of offering lucrative government projects to allies. Orbán has strongly denied the claims.

Two of his former ministers, including Seszták, and the former central bank chief Gyorgy Matolcsy have been under arrest since September over accusations of graft in separate investigations. They all deny wrongdoing.
On Monday, Hungarian authorities also detained Orbán's brother and three others as part of a people-smuggling case.
The former prime minister ​dismissed it as political revenge, saying: "In this dirty game, ​the aim is the elimination of the political opponent and the establishment of a one-party system.
"I am the target, my younger brother is just a tool."
I will serve - not rule over Hungary, says new PM
Hungary's president agrees to stand down after parliament backs removal
Hungary's public news broadcasts halted in bid to scrap Orban-era propaganda
body_zh: 图片来源，国家资产追回和保护办公室 (NVVH)
当局表示，在对欧尔班·维克多前部长的调查中，发现了近 2000 万美元（1480 万英镑）的现金藏在农场建筑中和埋在森林中。
米克洛什·塞斯塔克 (Miklós Seszták) 在这位前总理 16 年的任期中担任了四年的国家发展部长，他被指控收受贿赂，作为涉及国家运输公司的计划的一部分。他否认有任何不当行为。
匈牙利新任总理彼得·马扎尔 (Péter Magyar) 在 4 月份的选举中以压倒性优势击败了欧尔班，承诺将发起全面的反腐败运动。
周五，在对全国各地偏僻地点发现的现金进行了为期两天的搜寻之后，马扎尔将其描述为“黑手党”的终结。
国家资产追回和保护办公室（NVVH）在一份声明中表示，作为对塞什塔克调查的一部分，调查人员在保险箱、埋在林地、农业和住宅建筑及仓库中发现了大量钞票。
其补充称，现金总额为“5,071,632,000 福林、2,658,350 欧元和 1,257,100 美元”，总价值达到 1,950 万美元。该机构表示，这笔资金已存入匈牙利国库。
NVVH 的成立是为了调查欧尔班统治期间的腐败指控，马扎尔将其称为“炼狱行动”。
马扎尔在今年早些时候的选举中向匈牙利人承诺“政权更迭”，并自上任以来开始废除欧尔班时代的许多政策。
腐败和任人唯亲的指控长期以来一直困扰着欧尔班，他在任期内将匈牙利变成了欧盟所描述的“选举独裁国家”。
他的政府面临向盟友提供利润丰厚的政府项目的指控。欧尔班强烈否认了这些说法。
自9月份以来，他的两名前部长，包括塞斯塔克和前央行行长捷尔吉·马托尔奇，在单独的调查中因涉嫌贪污而被捕。他们都否认有不当行为。
周一，匈牙利当局还拘留了欧尔班的兄弟和其他三人，作为人口走私案件的一部分。
这位前总理将其斥为政治报复，并表示：“在这场肮脏的游戏中，目的是消灭政治对手并建立一党制。
“我才是目标，弟弟只是一个工具。”

title_en: 'Can you believe it?': SpaceX catches part of its Starship rocket on return to Earth
title_zh: “你能相信吗？”：SpaceX 在返回地球时捕获了其 Starship 火箭的一部分
summary: SpaceX has performed the historic catch using mechanical arms nicknamed "chopsticks".
summary_zh: SpaceX 使用绰号为“筷子”的机械臂完成了历史性的捕捉。
body_en: Watch: SpaceX catches part of its Starship rocket on return to Earth - BBC News
SpaceX has successfully caught the top part of its huge Starship rocket on its return to Earth for the first time.
"Can you believe it?," a commentator said as large crowds cheered at the launch site in Texas.
The company had hoped to catch both the bottom and upper stages of the rocket using mechanical arms - nicknamed chopsticks - on its launch tower.
But the first catch of the rocket's booster was aborted a few minutes after the launch on Friday. The booster was diverted to the ocean, bursting into flames just above the sea.
The top part, known as the Ship, returned to Earth a few minutes behind schedule at around 15:27 local time (21:27 GMT) on Saturday and was successfuly caught.
body_zh: 观看：SpaceX 在返回地球时捕获了其 Starship 火箭的一部分 - BBC 新闻
SpaceX 首次返回地球时成功抓住了其巨型 Starship 火箭的顶部。
“你能相信吗？”一名评论员说道，德克萨斯州的发射现场大批人群欢呼雀跃。
该公司曾希望使用发射塔上的机械臂（绰号“筷子”）抓住火箭的底部和上部阶段。
但火箭助推器的第一次捕获在周五发射几分钟后就中止了。助推器被转移到海洋，在海面上方起火。
周六当地时间 15 点 27 分（格林威治标准时间 21 点 27 分）左右，被称为“飞船”的顶部部分返回地球，并被成功捕获。

title_en: Nigeria's upcoming election marred by rising AI disinformation
title_zh: 尼日利亚即将举行的选举因人工智能虚假信息的增加而受到损害
summary: As Nigeria inches closer to the 2027 polls, the use of artificial intelligence in the electoral process has prompted questions about integrity and institutional readiness. Can Nigerians trust their democratic processes?
summary_zh: 随着尼日利亚距离 2027 年大选越来越近，人工智能在选举过程中的使用引发了人们对诚信和制度的质疑。
body_en: Nigeria has just over two months to go until its general election, with incumbent Bola Tinubu running on a ticket focused on combating raging insecurity and resolving the nation's economic crisis . He faces off against former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and senior opposition figure Peter Obi.

The country's electoral body, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), recently released its preliminary voter's register, which reportedly is riddled with images believed to have been generated using artificial intelligence (AI) .

Among the telltale signs of AI usage were exaggerated facial features in images and inconsistencies on the electoral registers, such as duplicates of names and even identities of people who since the previous election had died.

The development raises concerns about the body's overall preparedness ahead of the country's upcoming 2027 general election. Instead of making the upcoming vote more transparent by allowing access to its procedures, INEC has come under fire amid broader controversies about the expanding influence of AI in elections across the continent.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Joash Amupitan, the chairman of the electoral commission, said the body is now investigating the development, focusing on discrepancies potentially created by AI use.

To this end, he announced the establishment of a dedicated unit to monitor AI-related threats, detect deepfakes and strengthen the integrity of the electoral process, warning that the credibility of the upcoming election could otherwise be under attack.

However, even prior to the proliferation of AI across Africa and the globe, this would not be the first time that Nigeria has found itself in the unfortunate position of having to deal with the circulation of fabricated images , doctored audio and fake videos online. In the run-up to the 2023 election , deepfakes falsely linking candidates to terror-related activities filled social media platforms.

These are often designed to promote certain candidates or to discredit opponents in a bid to influence public perception, which now with the use of AI could create disinformation campaigns of new proportions.
Artificial intelligence has various effects on voter behavior
Lois Ugbede, the assistant editor at the factchecking platform DUBAWA, told DW that "based on our monitoring so far, AI-driven disinformation is serious and is becoming commonplace."

"This could influence political discourse and voter behavior ahead of 2027 because we are already seeing parties using inflated crowds to show that they have a large followership or support," she added.

At the same time, rather than influencing the vote in favor of any particular candidate, "the deeper danger is that people may begin to doubt authentic information simply because they know convincing AI-generated fakes are possible," said Akintunde Babatunde, executive director of the Abuja-based Centre for Journalism, Innovation and Development.

"We often focus on the risk of people believing an AI-generated falsehood, but there is another problem where genuine evidence can be dismissed as AI-generated," he noted, citing instances of a lawmaker who recently made inflammatory remarks during a campaign rally — but then claimed the clips were manipulated.
Further pitfalls behind a lack of safeguards against AI

Chibuike Mgbeahuruike, an election consultant at the Centre for Democracy and Development, told DW that apart from the spread of synthetic content online, AI intrusion into the electoral commission's portal could also "undermine its institutional credibility, especially with the low level of confidence that we are already witnessing."

He added, however, that AI itself is not inherently a threat to electoral integrity. The real threat lies in "the absence of effective accountability for its deployment," as innovations in tech increasingly appear to infiltrate governments and their democratic processes.
"Voters must have confidence … that the technology is also transparent, accountable and independently scrutinized, and ultimately subject to human and institutional oversight," said Mgbeahuruike.

Mallam Jibrin Baba Ndace, the director-general of state-owned broadcaster Voice of Nigeria, agrees, urging journalists at a recent conference also to not fall into the trap of believing reports, which later could turn out to be false due to AI manipulation.
body_zh: 距离尼日利亚大选只剩下两个多月的时间，现任总统博拉·蒂努布的竞选重点是消除严重的不安全局势并解决该国的经济危机。他与前副总统阿提库·阿布巴卡尔和高级反对派人物彼得·奥比对峙。
该国选举机构国家独立选举委员会（INEC）最近发布了初步选民登记册，据报道，登记册上充斥着据信是使用人工智能（AI）生成的图像。
人工智能使用的明显迹象包括图像中夸张的面部特征和选举登记册上的不一致，例如自上次选举以来已去世的人的姓名甚至身份重复。
这一事态发展引发了人们对该机构在该国即将到来的 2027 年大选之前的整体准备情况的担忧。由于人工智能在非洲大陆选举中影响力不断扩大的广泛争议，INEC 并没有通过允许访问其程序来使即将到来的投票更加透明，而是受到了批评。
要观看此视频，请启用 JavaScript，并考虑升级到支持 HTML5 视频的网络浏览器
选举委员会主席乔什·阿穆皮坦表示，该机构正在调查事态发展，重点关注人工智能的使用可能造成的差异。
为此，他宣布成立一个专门部门来监控人工智能相关威胁、检测深度造假并加强选举过程的完整性，并警告说，否则即将举行的选举的可信度可能会受到攻击。
然而，即使在人工智能在非洲和全球范围内扩散之前，尼日利亚也不是第一次发现自己处于不得不应对网上伪造图像、篡改音频和虚假视频传播的不幸境地。在 2023 年大选前夕，社交媒体平台上充斥着将候选人与恐怖相关活动错误联系起来的深度造假内容。
这些通常旨在宣传某些候选人或抹黑对手，以影响公众的看法，而现在，随着人工智能的使用，这可能会造成新规模的虚假信息活动。
人工智能对选民行为有多种影响
事实核查平台 DUBAWA 的助理编辑洛伊丝·乌格贝德 (Lois Ugbede) 告诉德国之声，“根据我们迄今为止的监测，人工智能驱动的虚假信息非常严重，而且正在变得司空见惯。”
“这可能会影响 2027 年之前的政治言论和选民行为，因为我们已经看到政党利用膨胀的人群来表明他们拥有大量的追随者或支持，”她补充道。
与此同时，阿布贾新闻、创新与发展中心执行主任阿金通德·巴巴通德 (Akintunde Babatunde) 表示，“更深层次的危险是，人们可能会开始怀疑真实信息，因为他们知道人工智能可能会生成令人信服的虚假信息，而不是影响对任何特定候选人的投票”。
他指出：“我们经常关注人们相信人工智能生成的谎言的风险，但还有另一个问题，即真实的证据可能会被视为人工智能生成而被驳回。”他引用了一位立法者的例子，该议员最近在一次竞选集会上发表了煽动性言论，但随后声称这些剪辑被操纵了。
缺乏人工智能保障措施背后的更多陷阱
民主与发展中心的选举顾问奇布伊克·姆贝阿鲁伊克 (Chibuike Mgbeahuruike) 告诉德国之声，除了网上合成内容的传播之外，人工智能对选举委员会门户网站的入侵也可能“损害其机构可信度，尤其是在我们已经目睹的信任度较低的情况下”。
不过，他补充说，人工智能本身并不是对选举公正性的固有威胁。真正的威胁在于“缺乏对其部署的有效问责”，因为技术创新似乎越来越多地渗透到政府及其民主进程中。
Mgbeahuruike 表示：“选民必须有信心……该技术也是透明的、负责任的、独立审查的，并最终受到人类和机构的监督。”
国有广播公司尼日利亚之声的总干事马拉姆·吉布林·巴巴·恩达斯 (Mallam Jibrin Baba Ndace) 对此表示同意，他在最近的一次会议上敦促记者不要陷入相信报道的陷阱，这些报道后来可能会因人工智能操纵而被证明是虚假的。

title_en: 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All passengers rescued after New Orleans cruise ship collision
title_zh: “密西西比奇迹”——新奥尔良游轮相撞后所有乘客均获救
summary: The collision leaves 32 people in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for.
summary_zh: 此次碰撞导致 32 人受伤入院，但无人下落不明。
body_en: Some 130 people on a cruise ship docked in New Orleans have been rescued after it was struck by a tanker.
The cruise ship, American Heritage, was left lying on its side in the Mississippi River after it was hit by the cargo vessel Atlantic Asphalt.
The collision left 32 people from the stricken riverboat in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for. Officials hailed it as a "miracle on the Mississippi".
The exact cause of the crash remains under investigation, but US Coast Guard Capt Melanie Burnham said: "There seems to be some type of a loss of steering."
New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno told a news conference on Friday that all credit in the rescue effort should go to first responders who "literally jumped right in to help".
"We have zero people unaccounted for, which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi," Moreno said.

Calls about the collision began around 13:30 EST (18:30 GMT) on Friday, when people began trying to help passengers escape the boat as it took on water, Port of New Orleans chief Melanie Montroll told the news conference.
Were you in the area at the time of incident? Get in touch .
There were about 129 passengers, in addition to crew members, on the American Heritage at the time of the collision, according to the port authority.
Passengers began getting off the paddlewheeler vessel, operated by American Cruise Lines, as it started listing before tipping onto its side, Moreno said.
Tugboat operators, police and other rescuers rushed to help while officials shut down traffic in the Mississippi River during the rescue effort.
The American Heritage had been finishing an eight-day cruise calling at destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi along the waterway.
On Saturday, Moreno said that nine people are still in hospital.
She said that the captain of the ship was injured in the accident but refused medical treatment until he knew all passengers and crew were accounted for.
US President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that the rescue had been an "incredible job".
Governor Jeff Landry also hailed the rescue as a "miracle on the Mississippi" given the "sheer number of people who were on that cruise ship" who were rescued.
Ships have operated safely on the Mississippi River for years, Landry said, pledging to investigate what had occurred.
Still covered in dirt from the boat crash, Joe Knab of Kansas told New Orleans NBC affiliate WDSU that the ship quickly capsized after the collision.
He spent about 20 minutes in the water before being rescued.
"When we first went in we were bobbing underneath the water; it was sinking pretty fast, but we finally got out of there," he said.
body_zh: 一艘停靠在新奥尔良的游轮被一艘油轮撞上，船上约130人已获救。
这艘游轮“美国遗产号”在被大西洋沥青号货船撞上后，侧躺在密西西比河中。
此次碰撞导致受损河船上的 32 人被送往医院，伤势不重，但无人下落不明。官员们称赞这是“密西西比河上的奇迹”。
坠机的确切原因仍在调查中，但美国海岸警卫队上尉梅兰妮·伯纳姆表示：“似乎存在某种类型的转向损失。”
新奥尔良市市长海伦娜·莫雷诺在周五的新闻发布会上表示，救援工作的所有功劳都应该归功于“真正立即投入帮助”的急救人员。
莫雷诺说：“我们有零人下落不明，这确实是密西西比河上的一个奇迹。”
新奥尔良港负责人梅兰妮·蒙特罗尔 (Melanie Montroll) 在新闻发布会上表示，有关碰撞的电话于周五 13:30（格林尼治标准时间 18:30）左右开始出现，当时人们开始试图帮助乘客在船进水时逃生。
事发时您在该地区吗？取得联系。
据港务局称，事故发生时，美国遗产号上除船员外，还有大约 129 名乘客。
莫雷诺说，这艘由美国邮轮公司运营的明轮船开始倾斜，然后侧翻，乘客们开始下船。
拖船操作员、警察和其他救援人员赶来提供帮助，同时官员在救援过程中关闭了密西西比河的交通。
美国遗产号已经结束了为期八天的航行，沿途停靠路易斯安那州和密西西比州的目的地。
周六，莫雷诺表示，仍有九人仍在医院接受治疗。
她说，船长在事故中受伤，但拒绝接受治疗，直到他知道所有乘客和船员都已下落不明。
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在《真相社会》上发帖称，救援工作是“令人难以置信的工作”。
州长杰夫·兰德里也称赞这次救援是“密西西比河上的奇迹”，因为获救的“游轮上的人数之多”。
兰德里说，船只多年来一直在密西西比河上安全运营，并承诺调查所发生的事情。
堪萨斯州的乔·纳布 (Joe Knab) 仍沾满沉船事故的污垢，他告诉新奥尔良 NBC 附属机构 WDSU，船在碰撞后很快就倾覆了。
他在水中待了大约20分钟才被救出。
“当我们第一次进去时，我们在水下漂浮；下沉得很快，但我们终于离开了那里，”他说。

title_en: Gen Z protests: Do Baby Boomers really have it better than young people?
title_zh: Z世代抗议：婴儿潮一代真的比年轻人过得更好吗？
summary: Should young people in Germany be more worried about their future than Baby Boomers were in the 1980s and 1990s? Or should both generations take to the streets and protest together? DW checked the data.
summary_zh: 德国的年轻人是否应该比 20 世纪 80 年代和 90 年代的婴儿潮一代更担心自己的未来？或者两代人都应该采取行动
body_en: Young people across Germany and Europe are taking to the streets, voicing fears of a bleak future.
But is that really the case? Does Gen Z face greater challenges than Baby Boomers did in the 1990s? What do the two generations have in common, and where do their experiences differ?

"Of course, it's fair to ask, 'Were things just as tough for you back then?'" youth researcher Simon Schnetzer tells DW. "But young people see that things are difficult for them now, and say that's why they need support today."

Schnetzer, who wrote the annual Youth in Germany study, highlights one key question raised by the recent demonstrations across Europe as: "Have we given young people the conditions they need to live and work here with confidence, and to keep this system funded?"

His straightforward answer is no. A survey of the statistics shows that both Gen Z and the Baby Boomers are affected by major societal changes, but in different ways. DW surveyed data on pensions, education, housing and climate change to find out more.

The facts point to a clear trend: Fewer and fewer young people are having to support an ever-growing number of retirees . According to the Germany's public pension insurance system, there were 3.73 contributors for every retiree in 1957. By 2025, that figure had fallen to just 2.1.
By 2045, this number is projected to drop to just 1.73 contributors per retiree. In absolute terms, this means 35.35 million contributors will be financing pensions for 16.82 million retirees.

To cushion this trend and keep contribution rates stable, the pension system already receives around €118 billion [$131 billion] in annual government subsidies. This amounts to roughly 25% of the federal budget. That means an increasing share of the population will be called upon to help fund pensions.

There are also signs that many people's pensions are already falling short of covering their living expenses. The number of retirees relying on federal basic income support has risen from 257,000 in 2003 to 738,000 in 2024.
What Germans young and old think about the pension system
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Rising rents hit low-income households particularly hard. According to a report by the German Institute for Economic Research (DIW), the share of income spent on rent by low-income households rose from around 24% in 1990 to nearly 36% in 2021.
This means that in 2021, the lowest-income households spent an average of 14 percentage points more of their income on rent than high-income households.

According to Germany's Federal Statistical Office (Destatis) , in 2025, an average of 11% of the population spent more than 40% of their disposable income on housing costs. Among people at risk of poverty, the figure was as high as 35%.

However, according to calculations by real estate platform Jacasa, Boomers could actually help ease pressure on the housing market in the coming years. They currently own around 4.8 million owner-occupied houses and apartments.

Over the coming decades, these properties are expected to change hands as former occupants sell them, move into assisted living, or hand them down through inheritance. In some regions, this could lead to an oversupply of properties and, consequently, lower prices, according to Jacasa's projections.

According to the federal government's Education Finance Report, public spending on education for people under 30 has doubled since 2011, rising from around €4,000 to approximately €8,000 per person annually.

Despite this increase, Germany ranks only in the middle of the pack internationally. According to the Federal Statistical Office (Destatis), public education spending accounted for 4.6% of Germany's gross domestic product (GDP) in 2022, compared with an OECD average of 4.7%.

However, the additional funding cannot solve the problem of teacher shortages. According to estimates by the Standing Conference of the Ministers of Education and Cultural Affairs, Germany will be short of around 27,000 teachers by 2035. The main reasons are the wave of Baby Boomer retirements and declining birth rates, which have contributed to a shortage of young teachers.

body_zh: 德国和欧洲各地的年轻人走上街头，表达对黯淡未来的恐惧。
但事实真的是这样吗？ Z 世代面临的挑战是否比 20 世纪 90 年代婴儿潮一代面临的挑战更大？两代人有什么共同点，他们的经历又有何不同？
“当然，我们可以公平地问，‘当时的情况对你来说也同样艰难吗？’”青年研究员西蒙·施内泽（Simon Schnetzer）告诉德国之声。 “但年轻人看到现在的事情对他们来说很困难，并说这就是他们今天需要支持的原因。”
施奈策撰写了年度德国青年研究报告，他强调了最近欧洲各地示威活动提出的一个关键问题：“我们是否为年轻人提供了他们自信地在这里生活和工作所需的条件，并为这个系统提供了资金支持？”
他直接的回答是否定的。一项统计调查显示，Z 世代和婴儿潮一代都受到重大社会变革的影响，但影响方式不同。德国之声调查了养老金、教育、住房和气候变化方面的数据，以了解更多信息。
The facts point to a clear trend: Fewer and fewer young people are having to support an ever-growing number of retirees .根据德国公共养老保险制度，1957年，每名退休人员有3.73人缴费。到2025年，这一数字已降至2.1人。
到 2045 年，这一数字预计将下降至每名退休人员仅 1.73 名缴款人。从绝对数量来看，这意味着 3535 万缴款人将为 1682 万退休人员提供养老金。
为了缓解这一趋势并保持缴费率稳定，养老金制度已获得约 1,180 亿欧元（1,310 亿美元）的年度政府补贴。这大约相当于联邦预算的 25%。这意味着越来越多的人口将被要求为养老金提供资金。
还有迹象表明，许多人的养老金已经不足以支付他们的生活费用。依赖联邦基本收入支持的退休人员人数已从 2003 年的 257,000 人增加到 2024 年的 738,000 人。
德国年轻人和老年人如何看待养老金制度

租金上涨对低收入家庭的打击尤其严重。德国经济研究所（DIW）的一份报告显示，低收入家庭用于租金的收入比例从1990年的24%左右上升到2021年的近36%。
这意味着，2021年，最低收入家庭用于租金的支出占其收入的平均比高收入家庭多14个百分点。
根据德国联邦统计局（Destatis）的数据，2025年，平均有11%的人口将可支配收入的40%以上用于住房费用。在面临贫困风险的人群中，这一数字高达35%。
然而，根据房地产平台 Jacasa 的计算，婴儿潮一代实际上可以帮助缓解未来几年房地产市场的压力。他们目前拥有约 480 万套自住房屋和公寓。
在未来的几十年里，随着前居住者出售它们、进入辅助生活区或通过继承将它们传下来，这些房产预计将易手。根据 Jacasa 的预测，在某些地区，这可能会导致房地产供应过剩，从而导致价格下降。
根据联邦政府的教育财政报告，自 2011 年以来，30 岁以下人群的公共教育支出翻了一番，从每人每年约 4,000 欧元增加到约 8,000 欧元。
尽管有这样的增长，德国在国际上的排名仅处于中游。根据联邦统计局(Destatis)的数据，2022年公共教育支出占德国国内生产总值(GDP)的4.6%，而经合组织的平均水平为4.7%。
然而，追加经费并不能解决师资短缺的问题。据教育和文化部长常务会议估计，到2035年，德国将短缺约2.7万名教师。主要原因是婴儿潮一代退休潮和出生率下降导致年轻教师短缺。
早在 1972 年，罗马俱乐部就在其具有里程碑意义的出版物《增长的极限》中警告了全球变暖的后果。据联合国称，到本世纪末，与工业化前水平相比，地球气温将上升 2.6°C。

title_en: More than 100,000 rally across France in new Yellow Vest protests
title_zh: 法国各地超过10万人集会参加新的黄背心抗议活动
summary: Protesters chanted against declining affordability, the Macron government, police violence and poor school conditions.
summary_zh: 抗议者高喊反对负担能力下降、马克龙政府、警察暴力和恶劣的学校条件。
body_en: More than 100,000 rally across France in new Yellow Vest protests | Protests News | Al Jazeera
Share More than 100,000 rally across France in new Yellow Vest protests on social media
More than 100,000 people have taken to the streets in France in another round of cost-of-living rallies organised by the “Yellow Vests” and various youth movements.
Saturday’s protests saw a decline in turnout compared with previous weekends and stayed largely calm, authorities said.

list 2 of 3 Mapping how France’s protest wave spread across Europe
list 3 of 3 France accelerates minimum wage hike in bid to quell protest

The Ministry of the Interior reported that 106,000 people took part in protests nationwide, including 24,000 in Paris – down from 146,000 people nationwide and 46,000 in Paris last week. Student unions place Saturday’s protest numbers higher, at 200,000 people, including almost 100,000 in the capital.

The country has been gripped by high-school blockades, mass demonstrations, and strikes for more than a month, with protesters rallying against falling educational standards, cost-of-living increases, low wages, and police violence.
A number of demonstrators also carried signs targeting President Emmanuel Macron, who has faced significant criticism from protesters.

Some rallies in recent weeks have seen violence at the fringes, and the first major protest on October 17 saw looting in cities across France. Since then, police presence at rallies and controls on transport and permits to protest have been expanded.

Marseille, France’s second-largest city, banned protests over the weekend, but the prefecture announced that some 3,500 people still took to the streets. Local media reported that tear gas and a water cannon were used against protesters and shared images of fires burning in a popular local square.

In Lyon, local media reported that roughly 8,000 people took to the streets. They shared images of masked protesters chanting in front of fires lit in the street and police charging and using tear gas.
Tear gas use was also reported in Nantes, Bordeaux and Paris.
Unions have called for a new day of strikes on Tuesday after rejecting a government promise to increase the minimum wage by 0.6 percent as “crumbs”.

If the demonstrations go ahead, they will take place on the eighth anniversary of the Gilet Jaune – which translates to “Yellow Vest” in French – movement, which rocked the beginning of the Macron government in 2018 with two years of protests triggered by rising fuel prices.

On Tuesday, the Yellow Vests will “celebrate their eight years where it all started: on roundabouts and toll booths all over France”, Yellow Vest protest tracking website 17octobregiletjaune.net writes.

法国第二大城市马赛周末禁止抗议活动，但该地区宣布仍有约 3,500 人走上街头。当地媒体报道称，警方对抗议者使用了催泪瓦斯和高压水枪，并分享了当地一个受欢迎的广场发生火灾的图像。

title_en: Tens of thousands march in latest Portugal housing protests
title_zh: 葡萄牙最新住房抗议活动中数万人游行
summary: These were the biggest protests against rising housing costs in Portugal since the social movement began weeks ago.
summary_zh: 这是自几周前社会运动开始以来葡萄牙针对住房成本上涨最大规模的抗议活动。
body_en: Share Tens of thousands march in latest Portugal housing protests on social media
By Al Jazeera Staff , Anadolu and The Associated Press

Tens of thousands of people have taken to the streets of more than 30 towns and cities in Portugal to protest against surging rental prices, demanding urgent government action to address the country’s worsening housing crisis.

Organised by the Casa Para Viver (A Home to Live In) platform, demonstrations on Saturday took place under the slogan “They will not steal our right to a home,” with protests in Lisbon, Porto, Faro, Portimao, Coimbra, Braga and other locations. It was the biggest national demonstration since the social movement began weeks ago .

list 2 of 4 Portugal cost-of-living protesters pour back into camps cleared by police
list 3 of 4 Portuguese police clear Lisbon housing protest camp, arrest 25
list 4 of 4 Police storm Portugal housing protest camp

Participants, ranging from teenagers to retired people, walked behind large banners, with the Lisbon march punctuated by drums, music, and chanting. Protesters called for caps to be placed on rent increases, greater legal protection for tenants against eviction, and more affordable housing. They also demanded the reversal of proposed changes to rental legislation.
One woman on a protest march in Lisbon told Al Jazeera that she was a business owner, “and I can’t afford a house.”
“I can’t say much more than this. I’m forty-years-old, I can’t go to a bank and just buy a house with my money,” she added.
Another woman told Al Jazeera that she had joined the march to protest “for a better life, for all of us, not just the young people, all of us, because we deserve to have a home.”

One man told Al Jazeera “we have been suffering this for the last three or four years, and I have many friends and family in this situation, they had to move because they cannot afford the rent. If you earn, for example, a thousand euros, and you have to pay rent of six hundred, seven hundred, then you cannot live, it’s impossible.”

Casa Para Vivir brings together approximately 100 housing associations and grassroots organisations, is seeking tighter regulation on rental contracts, short-term tourist accommodation, and vacant properties.
The protests come after parliament approved the government’s proposed changes to provide greater flexibility in rental contracts and accelerate eviction procedures.
Housing campaigners warned the changes could weaken tenant protections amid rising rents and limited housing availability.

House prices in Portugal have risen much faster than incomes in recent years, statistics show. Between 2015 and 2025, Portugal posted the biggest jump in the European Union in the home price-to-income ratio, with an increase of 61 percent, followed by the Netherlands with 34 percent, the EU statistical office Eurostat said last week.

There is no indication that the rise in housing costs is slowing. Between the first quarter of last year and the first quarter of 2026, property prices rose by almost 20 percent, the National Statistics Institute, a government agency, said last month.

Rental prices, too, have climbed significantly, recording a 68 percent increase since 2020, according to the government. Much of this jump in real estate costs has been fuelled by foreign buyers and investment funds, as the country’s relaxed climate near the ocean has attracted many remote workers and retirees.

The government has responded to the protests by lowering taxes on new construction, restricting short-term rentals, and promising to build 145,000 new homes, but it acknowledged that the effects will not be immediate, as Prime Minister Luis Montenegro was urged by Casa Para Viver representatives to engage directly with them.

周六，由Casa Para Viver（居住之家）平台组织的示威活动以“他们不会窃取我们的住房权”为口号，在里斯本、波尔图、法鲁、波尔蒂芒、科英布拉、布拉加和其他地点举行了抗议活动。这是自几周前社会运动开始以来最大规模的全国示威活动。

参加者从青少年到退休人员，都走在巨大的横幅后面，里斯本游行的鼓声、音乐和口号不绝于耳。抗议者呼吁对租金上涨设定上限，为租户提供更大的法律保护，防止他们被驱逐，并提供更多经济适用房。他们还要求撤销对租赁立法的拟议修改。
里斯本抗议游行中的一名妇女告诉半岛电视台，她是一名企业主，“我买不起房子。”
“我不能说的更多了。我已经四十岁了，我不能去银行用我的钱买房子，”她补充道。
另一位妇女告诉半岛电视台，她参加游行是为了“为了我们所有人的更好生活，不仅仅是年轻人，而是我们所有人，因为我们应该拥有一个家。”
一名男子告诉半岛电视台：“过去三四年来，我们一直在遭受这种痛苦，我有很多朋友和家人面临这种​​情况，他们不得不搬家，因为他们付不起房租。如果你赚了，例如，一千欧元，而你必须支付六百、七百欧元的租金，那么你就无法生活，这是不可能的。”
Casa Para Vivir 汇集了大约 100 个住房协会和基层组织，正在寻求对租赁合同、短期旅游住宿和空置房产进行更严格的监管。
抗议活动是在议会批准政府提议的改革之后发生的，该改革旨在为租赁合同提供更大的灵活性并加快驱逐程序。
住房活动人士警告称，在租金上涨和住房供应有限的情况下，这些变化可能会削弱对租户的保护。
统计数据显示，近年来葡萄牙房价的上涨速度远远快于收入的上涨速度。欧盟统计局上周表示，2015 年至 2025 年间，葡萄牙的房价收入比在欧盟中增幅最大，增长了 61%，其次是荷兰，增长了 34%。
没有迹象表明住房成本的上涨正在放缓。政府机构国家统计局上个月表示，从去年第一季度到 2026 年第一季度，房价上涨了近 20%。
据政府称，租金价格也大幅上涨，自 2020 年以来上涨了 68%。房地产成本的上涨很大程度上是由外国买家和投资基金推动的，因为该国靠近海洋的宽松气候吸引了许多远程工人和退休人员。
政府通过降低新建建筑税、限制短期租金并承诺建造 145,000 套新房来应对抗议活动，但承认效果不会立竿见影，因为 Casa Para Viver 代表敦促总理路易斯·黑山直接与他们接触。

title_en: Copper wire upgrade caused nationwide flight suspension, US transport secretary says
title_zh: 美国运输部长称铜线升级导致全国航班停飞
summary: The US government is trying to find out whether the chaos was caused by "incompetence" or faulty equipment.
summary_zh: 美国政府正试图查明这场混乱是由“无能”还是设备故障造成的。
body_en: Copper wire upgrade caused nationwide flight chaos, US transport secretary says - BBC News
A nationwide US ground stop that caused thousands of flight cancellations was caused by an issue following a copper wire upgrade, Transport Secretary Sean Duffy said.
Duffy told a news conference that the government was trying to find out whether the problem was caused by "incompetence" on the part of the company doing the upgrades, or faulty equipment.
The US government does not believe it was as a result of a cyber-attack, although an investigation is still under way, Duffy said.
Friday's suspension was the longest such incident since the 11 September 2001 attacks on the US and the disruption is expected to last for days.
Maintenance was being carried out to switch from copper wire to fibre by a contractor called L3Harris, a technology provider company, Duffy said.
The US has "an incredibly old telecommunications system", he added.
"It was such an old wire that it was being discontinued," he said.

The transport secretary explained that a router that was being worked on had started flooding other air traffic control systems and created communication issues with planes which led the government to shut down the airspace for safety reasons.
Bryan Bedford, who heads the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), told the same news conference: "We see zero evidence of anything nefarious, and zero evidence of anything AI related."
On Saturday L3Harris said it had completed over 70% of the work to modernise communications infrastructure before the shutdown.
"We are supporting the FAA in its investigation to understand the conditions that led to the 13 November ground stop of our nation's air travel," it said in a statement.
"L3Harris takes the nationwide ground stop and its impact on travellers, airlines and air traffic operations seriously."
No flights were allowed to take off from the continental US for more than four hours from 15:54 EST (19:54 GMT) on Friday.
More than 3,500 flights were cancelled and more than 2,000 delayed in the US on Saturday, according to tracking website Flight Aware, as knock-on disruption continues.

In some cases, passengers were left stuck inside planes on the tarmac, unable to take off or to return to the gates. Some international flights were allowed to depart US airports, in an apparent effort to clear space.
Duffy warned that a similar issue could arise again unless the US Congress approved upgrades to air traffic control infrastructure.
US President Donald Trump has requested $30.1bn for the upgrades. Both chambers of Congress are currently controlled by the Republican Party.

Former TSA Administrator John Pistole told the BBC that "the fact that they were able to get it restarted in four-and-a-half hours is good news - it shows a resilience in the system - but what's to say it's not going to happen tomorrow?"
A nationwide ground stop has only been ordered one other time since all flights were banned from take-off for several days following the 11 September 2001 attacks.
body_zh: 美国运输部长称铜线升级导致全国航班混乱 -_澳门赌博平台
运输部长肖恩·达菲表示，美国全国范围内的一次地面停靠导致数千架航班取消，原因是铜线升级后出现问题。
达菲在新闻发布会上表示，政府正在试图查明问题是否是由于进行升级的公司“无能”或设备故障造成的。
达菲表示，美国政府不认为这是网络攻击造成的，但调查仍在进行中。
周五的中断是自 2001 年 9 月 11 日美国遭受袭击以来最长的此类事件，预计中断将持续数天。
Duffy 表示，一家名为 L3Harris 的技术提供商公司承包商正在进行维护工作，以从铜线切换到光纤。
他补充说，美国拥有“极其古老的电信系统”。
“这是一种非常旧的电线，以至于已经停产了，”他说。
交通部长解释说，正在开发的路由器已经开始淹没其他空中交通管制系统，并造成与飞机的通信问题，导致政府出于安全原因关闭了空域。
美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 负责人布莱恩·贝德福德 (Bryan Bedford) 在同一场新闻发布会上表示：“我们看到任何邪恶行为的证据为零，任何与人工智能相关的证据也为零。”
周六，L3Harris 表示，在关闭之前，该公司已完成了 70% 以上的通信基础设施现代化工作。
美国联邦航空局在一份声明中表示：“我们正在支持美国联邦航空局进行调查，以了解导致我国航空旅行于 11 月 13 日地面停止的原因。”
“L3Harris 严肃对待全国范围内的地面停靠及其对旅客、航空公司和空中交通运营的影响。”
自周五美国东部时间 15:54（格林尼治标准时间 19:54）起超过四个小时，不允许任何航班从美国大陆起飞。
根据跟踪网站 Flight Aware 的数据，周六，美国有 3,500 多个航班被取消，2,000 多个航班延误，连锁干扰仍在继续。
在某些情况下，乘客被困在停机坪上的飞机内，无法起飞或返回登机口。一些国际航班被允许从美国机场起飞，显然是为了腾出空间。
达菲警告说，除非美国国会批准升级空中交通管制基础设施，否则类似的问题可能会再次出现。
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普已要求拨款 301 亿美元用于升级。目前国会参众两院均由共和党控制。
运输安全管理局前局长约翰·皮斯托尔 (John Pistole) 告诉 BBC，“他们能够在四个半小时内重新启动系统，这是个好消息 - 它显示了系统的弹性 - 但怎么能说明天就不会发生呢？”
自 2001 年 9 月 11 日袭击事件发生后数天所有航班均禁止起飞以来，仅曾下令在全国范围内进行一次地面停飞。

title_en: Philippines’ Carmelle wins first Eurovision contest in Asia
title_zh: 菲律宾的卡梅尔赢得了亚洲首届欧洲歌唱大赛冠军
summary: Filipino entry, pop and rap song Sobra-Sobra, takes 19-year-old to victory at grand final in Bangkok Carmelle Collado has won the first Eurovision song contest Asia, taking the Philippines’ entry, Sobra-Sobra , to victory in Bangkok on Saturday night, at the f
summary_zh: 菲律宾参赛歌曲、流行和说唱歌曲 Sobra-Sobra 带领 19 岁少年在曼谷总决赛中获胜 卡梅尔·科拉多 (Carmelle Collado) 赢得了第一个欧洲歌唱大赛冠军
body_en: Filipino entry, pop and rap song Sobra-Sobra, takes 19-year-old to victory at grand final in Bangkok

Carmelle Collado has won the first Eurovision song contest Asia, taking the Philippines’ entry, Sobra-Sobra , to victory in Bangkok on Saturday night, at the first regional edition of the contest to be staged outside Europe.
Eleven countries competed at the One Bangkok Forum in central Bangkok, and the show ran for two and a half hours including advertising.

The winner, who performs under the single name Carmelle, finished on 211 points, 41 clear of the hosts Thailand , with Vietnam third. She received the most votes from both the national juries and the public ballot.
Carmelle, 19, grew up beside the railway tracks in the Bicol region of south-eastern Luzon and has been competing in televised talent contests since she was 12.
Sobra-Sobra mixes pop and rap, is supported by traditional Philippine instruments, the kubing and kulintang, and is sung in Tagalog and English.
After her victory, Carmelle said her song celebrated female empowerment and was intended as “a tribute to all Filipino women”.
“I made history, since this was the first time,” she told the Associated Press. “It’s such a big responsibility for me, because this one is a global stage, so thank you everybody who voted for me.”
“It’s about how unapologetic, independent and strong Filipinas are,” she told the Guardian before the final. “It describes me – not just me, but of course all the Filipinas.”

The show opened with a routine celebrating the host country, in which Muay Thai fighters shared the stage with drag performers on street food carts. The 11 acts were then driven on in tuk-tuks, each carrying their national flag.

Vietnam’s Tóc Tiên , a star at home for more than 20 years, performed first, among dancers costumed as lotus leaves. Mang x Daou represented Thailand, a duo assembled for the contest in the host country who performed a duet staged like a musical number.

Nepal’s Pratik Himal Rai gave one of the most conventionally Eurovision performances of the night with Ananta Maya , a rock ballad staged with fire imagery and a large heart-shaped structure behind him.

He ended it by appealing for support for his country, which he said was “going [through a] very hard situation”. More than 1,500 people were killed and more than 5,000 were reported missing after a rock and ice avalanche near the Chinese border triggered catastrophic flash floods in August.

Bangladesh’s Beatmosphere , originally a nine-member a cappella and beatbox group, sang without a single instrument. Three of their members were left out of the final due to a rule capping each act at six performers on stage.
Nyendra from Bhutan sang dressed in the gho, his country’s national dress for men, against a backdrop of Himalayan peaks. Mongolia’s Beck performed in a reinterpreted deel, also a national costume.
Half the result was decided before the show began. The 11 national juries voted at a dress rehearsal on Friday night and put the Philippines at the top with 93 points, ahead of Vietnam and Malaysia.
The other half came from viewers around the world, who could vote online but not for their own country, and who were given eight free votes each and the option to buy 10 more.

Laos’s entrant, Thinla, was unable to hear her own music during her performance, and her dress rehearsal was aired once all live performances were over. She finished fifth, with the night’s third-highest public score.
Carmelle receives no prize money but does get a trophy presented by Dara, the Bulgarian singer who won this year’s European contest , and will perform at Eurovision 2027 in Burgas.
body_zh: 菲律宾选手、流行和说唱歌曲 Sobra-Sobra 带领 19 岁选手在曼谷总决赛中获胜
卡梅尔·科拉多 (Carmelle Collado) 赢得了首届欧洲歌唱大赛亚洲区冠军，周六晚，菲律宾歌曲《Sobra-Sobra》在曼谷举行，这是该大赛在欧洲以外举行的首届地区性比赛。
11 个国家参加了位于曼谷市中心的“同一个曼谷论坛”，比赛持续了两个半小时，其中还包括广告。
获胜者以卡梅尔（Carmelle）的名字参赛，最终获得 211 分，领先东道主泰国 41 分，越南队位居第三。她在国家评审团和公众投票中获得了最多的选票。
19 岁的卡梅尔在吕宋岛东南部比科尔地区的铁轨旁长大，从 12 岁起就开始参加电视才艺比赛。
Sobra-Sobra 混合了流行音乐和说唱音乐，由菲律宾传统乐器、古宾和库林堂伴奏，并用他加禄语和英语演唱。
卡梅尔获胜后表示，她的歌曲颂扬了女性赋权，旨在“向所有菲律宾女性致敬”。
“我创造了历史，因为这是第一次，”她告诉美联社。 “这对我来说是一项重大责任，因为这是一个全球舞台，所以感谢所有投票给我的人。”
“这是关于菲律宾人是多么的无悔、独立和坚强，”她在决赛前告诉《卫报》。 “它描述了我——不仅仅是我，当然还有所有菲律宾人。”
演出以庆祝主办国的例行仪式开始，泰拳战士与街头小吃车上的变装表演者同台表演。随后，这 11 名表演者乘坐嘟嘟车继续前行，每辆嘟嘟车上都挂着各自的国旗。
越南的 Tóc Tiên，一位在国内出道 20 多年的明星，首先在身着荷叶造型的舞者中表演。 Mang x Daou 代表泰国，这对组合在东道国参加比赛，表演了一场音乐剧般的二重唱。
尼泊尔的普拉蒂克·希马尔·拉伊 (Pratik Himal Rai) 与阿南塔·玛雅 (Ananta Maya) 进行了当晚最传统的欧洲歌唱大赛表演之一，这是一首摇滚民谣，上演了火焰图像，身后有一个巨大的心形结构。
最后他呼吁人们支持他的国家，他说这个国家“正在经历非常困难的局面”。 8 月份，中国边境附近的岩冰雪崩引发灾难性山洪，造成 1,500 多人死亡，5,000 多人失踪。
孟加拉国的 Beatmosphere 最初是一个由九名成员组成的无伴奏合唱和口技组合，在没有任何乐器的情况下演唱。由于舞台上每场表演的限制为六名表演者，他们的三名成员被排除在决赛之外。
来自不丹的 Nyendra 身穿 gho（不丹男性民族服饰），以喜马拉雅山峰为背景唱歌。蒙古的贝克穿着经过重新诠释的迪尔表演，这也是一种民族服装。
一半的结果在演出开始前就已经决定了。 11 个国家的评审团在周五晚上的彩排中投票，结果菲律宾以 93 分位居榜首，领先于越南和马来西亚。
另一半来自世界各地的观众，他们可以在线投票，但不能为自己的国家投票，每人获得八张免费选票，并可以选择购买另外十张选票。
老挝的参赛者Thinla在表演期间无法听到自己的音乐，所有现场表演结束后，她的彩排才得以播出。她获得第五名，获得当晚第三高的公共得分。
卡梅尔没有获得奖金，但获得了今年欧洲比赛冠军保加利亚歌手达拉颁发的奖杯，并将在布尔加斯举行的 2027 年欧洲歌唱大赛上进行表演。

title_en: Italy fines Meta €805m over accessing users' photos
title_zh: 意大利因访问用户照片而对 Meta 罚款 8.05 亿欧元
summary: The social media giant is accused of not informing 20 million users it had access to their photos.
summary_zh: 这家社交媒体巨头被指控没有通知 2000 万用户它有权访问他们的照片。
body_en: Italian regulators have fined social media giant Meta €805m (£670m; $887m) for accessing Android users' photos without their specific consent.
Italy's Data Protection Authority said Meta did not properly inform about 20 million smartphone users that it had access to their photos and videos via a feature of the Facebook app.
It has given Meta 60 days to disable the feature by default and seek users' consent separately.
The fine is among the largest an Italian authority has ever imposed on a tech giant.
A Meta spokesperson told the BBC that it planned to appeal.
The charge is related to a feature which suggests photos and videos from a user's phone gallery as ideas for posts.

Facebook requested access to users' photo galleries through a single app-wide authorisation. According to the Italian regulator, a preceding notice did not make clear that this would also allow Facebook to generate suggestions based on photos in their gallery.

The regulator said it took into account "the high number of people affected" and the fact it is "still ongoing for those who have not updated the app and for those who have already given their consent to the system".
Meta told the BBC: "We strongly disagree with the [regulator's] assessment of the facts, its application of the law, and the disproportionate level of the fine.

"This is a straightforward feature which helps people post photos and videos to Facebook. People must give permission on their device before it can operate, and they can change this permission at any time via their settings."
Last month, Meta, which is also behind Instagram and WhatsApp, was hit with its largest fine ever for its business practices.
A US judge in New Mexico ordered the company to pay $25bn (£18.6bn) after it found that found it had spent years lying to the public about how it handled Facebook user data.
body_zh: 意大利监管机构对社交媒体巨头 Meta 处以 8.05 亿欧元（6.7 亿英镑；8.87 亿美元）的罚款，原因是未经 Android 用户明确同意就访问其照片。
意大利数据保护局表示，Meta 没有正确告知约 2000 万智能手机用户，它可以通过 Facebook 应用程序的一项功能访问他们的照片和视频。
它给了 Meta 60 天的时间来默认禁用该功能并单独征求用户同意。
这是意大利当局有史以来对科技巨头处以的最大罚款之一。
Meta 发言人告诉 BBC，它计划上诉。
这笔费用与一项功能有关，该功能会建议用户手机图库中的照片和视频作为帖子的创意。
Facebook 请求通过单一应用程序范围的授权访问用户的照片库。据意大利监管机构称，之前的通知并未明确表明这也将允许 Facebook 根据其图库中的照片生成建议。
监管机构表示，它考虑到“受影响的人数很多”，以及“对于那些尚未更新应用程序的人和那些已经同意该系统的人来说，该计划仍在进行中”这一事实。
梅塔告诉英国广播公司：“我们强烈不同意（监管机构）对事实的评估、法律的适用以及不成比例的罚款。
“这是一个简单的功能，可以帮助人们将照片和视频发布到 Facebook。人们必须在设备上授予权限才能操作，并且可以随时通过设置更改此权限。”
上个月，Instagram 和 WhatsApp 背后的 Meta 因其商业行为而被处以有史以来最大的罚款。
新墨西哥州的一名美国法官发现该公司多年来在处理 Facebook 用户数据的方式上向公众撒谎，并命令该公司支付 250 亿美元（186 亿英镑）的赔偿金。

title_en: Fuel crisis and protests pressure Chile's far-right president
title_zh: 燃料危机和抗议给智利极右翼总统带来压力
summary: Chile's far-right President José Antonio Kast is facing mounting public anger, as rising fuel prices trigger transport strikes and protests across the country.
summary_zh: 智利极右翼总统何塞·安东尼奥·卡斯特面临公众日益高涨的愤怒，因为燃油价格上涨引发了全国各地的交通运输罢工和抗议活动。
body_en: Chile’s Kast faces growing protests as fuel prices soar and approval plunges : NPR

Chile’s Kast faces growing protests as fuel prices soar and approval plunges Chile's far-right President José Antonio Kast is facing mounting public anger, as rising fuel prices trigger transport strikes and protests across the country.

A masked demonstrator prepares to throw a Molotov cocktail as police use a water cannon to disperse students protesting education policies, rising living costs and reduced sentences for people convicted of sexual offenses against minors in Santiago, Chile, Nov. 5, 2026. Esteban Felix/AP hide caption
SANTIAGO, Chile — Chile's ultraconservative president finds himself on the back foot after just eight months in power.

José Antonio Kast, a politician who spent a career railing against progressive issues, reproductive rights and welfare policies from the extreme fringes of right-wing politics, now finds himself with just 24% approval in the polls.

It is less than a year since Kast stormed to the presidency in December 2025 by avoiding all mention of his hardline stances on social matters, focusing instead on two hot-button issues whipped up in the national media: illegal immigration and public security.
Chile turns right: Kast inaugurated as nation's most conservative leader since Pinochet
But rather than pressing ahead with those at the top of his agenda, he has floundered. And as elsewhere around the Americas and worldwide, rising costs of living have come to hit him hard.
"Our salaries are maybe 20% of a European income, but with a similar cost of living – it's terrible," said Simón Echavarría, a 30-year-old architect, at a march in Santiago on Friday evening.

"We want to protest against the measures that have set us back on environmental issues, on human rights, even reducing the sentences of pedophiles – they are implementing things that nobody asked for," he said.
Behind him, heavily armed police blocked the streets and fired water cannons at protesters chanting and waving flags in the square.

Much of the recent ire stems from the revelation last month that Kast's government had signed decrees to cut the sentences of 56 prisoners whose crimes range from the rape of children to dictatorship-era human rights violations.
Kast has since admitted that this was an "error", but came out in support of the undersecretary who signed the decrees nonetheless.
But beneath the more egregious moves Kast has made in his first year in power is simmering discontent over affordability.
In July, Kast's government chose not to apply an anti-inflation tool available to the Chilean state to ease the rise in fuel prices brought about by the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran.
Protests exploded as prices shot up overnight and motorists joined long queues at gas stations to fill their tanks before the rise came into effect.
Trucks are parked along a road as drivers protest rising fuel prices and operating costs on the outskirts of Santiago, Chile, Nov. 12, 2026. Esteban Felix/AP hide caption
This week, Chile's formidable truckers' unions blockaded two major highways in an effort to exert pressure on the government and address high fuel prices.
body_zh: 随着燃料价格飙升和批准率下降，智利卡斯特面临越来越多的抗议：NPR
随着燃料价格飙升和支持率暴跌，智利卡斯特面临越来越多的抗议 燃料价格上涨引发全国各地的交通运输罢工和抗议活动，智利极右翼总统何塞·安东尼奥·卡斯特面临着越来越高的公众愤怒。
2026 年 11 月 5 日，智利圣地亚哥，一名蒙面示威者准备投掷燃烧瓶，而警察则使用高压水枪驱散学生，抗议教育政策、生活成本上涨以及对未成年人性犯罪者减刑。Esteban Felix/美联社隐藏标题栏
智利圣地亚哥——智利极端保守的总统在上任仅八个月后就发现自己陷入了困境。
何塞·安东尼奥·卡斯特 (José Antonio Kast) 是一位政治家，他的职业生涯一直在反对右翼政治极端边缘的进步问题、生殖权利和福利政策，现在他发现自己在民意调查中的支持率仅为 24%。
距离卡斯特于 2025 年 12 月上任总统不到一年，他避免提及自己在社会问题上的强硬立场，而是将注意力集中在国家媒体上掀起的两个热点问题：非法移民和公共安全。
智利右转：卡斯特就任皮诺切特以来最保守的国家领导人
但他并没有继续推进他最重要的议程，而是陷入了困境。与美洲和世界其他地方一样，生活成本的上涨对他造成了沉重打击。
周五晚上，30 岁的建筑师西蒙·埃查瓦里亚 (Simón Echavarría) 在圣地亚哥的一次游行中表示：“我们的工资可能是欧洲人收入的 20%，但生活成本却相似，这太糟糕了。”
他说：“我们想要抗议那些在环境问题、人权问题上让我们倒退的措施，甚至减少恋童癖者的刑期——他们正在实施没有人要求的事情。”
在他身后，全副武装的警察封锁了街道，并向广场上高呼口号、挥舞旗帜的抗议者发射高压水枪。
最近的愤怒很大程度上源于上个月卡斯特政府签署法令对 56 名囚犯减刑的消息，这些囚犯的罪行包括强奸儿童和独裁时代侵犯人权等。
卡斯特此后承认这是一个“错误”，但仍然站出来支持签署这些法令的副部长。
但在卡斯特执政第一年采取的更令人震惊的举措背后，隐藏着对负担能力的不满。
7月，卡斯特政府选择不采用智利政府可用的反通胀工具，以缓解美以与伊朗战争带来的燃油价格上涨。
随着价格一夜之间飙升，驾车者在涨价生效之前在加油站排起长队加油，引发了抗议活动。
2026 年 11 月 12 日，智利圣地亚哥郊区，卡车停在路边，司机抗议不断上涨的燃油价格和运营成本。Esteban Felix/美联社隐藏标题栏
本周，智利强大的卡车司机工会封锁了两条主要高速公路，试图向政府施加压力并解决高油价问题。

title_en: Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week, White House says
title_zh: 白宫表示，特朗普、普京和习近平计划下周在中国举行历史性联席会议
summary: Trump will discuss the "reduction of nuclear weapons" during the unprecedented talks, a spokeswoman says.
summary_zh: 一位发言人表示，特朗普将在这次史无前例的会谈中讨论“削减核武器”问题。
body_en: Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping are planning to meet on the sidelines of a summit in China next week, the White House has said.

The historic meeting between the respective leaders of the US, Russia and China will take place as Trump attends the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation (Apec) summit in the southern city of Shenzhen, spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters.
"The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world, whose proliferation President Trump believes is very dangerous," she said.
It is understood Iran may also be discussed during the meeting of the world's biggest nuclear powers, but not Ukraine. Russia has confirmed the meeting. China has yet to react.
No agreement was expected to follow the talks, an unnamed, senior US official said, according to news agencies AP and Reuters.

Trump will arrive in Shenzhen late on Wednesday for the two-day summit between the 21 member states. He will also take part in bilateral talks with Xi on Thursday - their fourth meeting since the US president returned to office in 2025.

"President Trump will conclude his visit to China with a trilateral meeting between the president of the United States, the president of the People's Republic of China, and the president of the Russian Federation," Wales said.

She said Trump's trip, which will also include attending an Association of South-east Asian Nations (Asean) summit in the Philippines on Tuesday, would "secure historic wins to the American people and advance America's interests in the Indo Pacific".

A nuclear weapons control treaty between the US and Russia expired in February, leaving the world's biggest nuclear arsenals without major guardrails and effectively marking an end to the arms control co-operation that helped resolve the Cold War.
The UN has urged both sides to agree a new framework without delay. Trump however said he could replace the deal with a better agreement that included China , which has been building up its arsenal.
Former senior US officials and analysts told the BBC at the time that seeking Beijing and Moscow's co-operation could create major hurdles and take years.
Xi separately hosted both Putin and Trump in Beijing just days apart earlier this year, while the US president welcomed his Chinese counterpart to Washington in September.
Beijing has become a crucial trading partner for Moscow since it launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, which has isolated Russia and left it subject to Western sanctions.

But a controversial US deal to import Russian diesel and the suspension of sanctions targeting the biggest buyers of Moscow's oil and gas - including China - heightened European concern about the Trump administration's softening towards the Kremlin last month.

Trump and Xi have meanwhile sought to project warmer ties at summits in Beijing and Washington this year - though little significant progress appeared to have been made on key issues such as trade, their race for AI dominance, and Taiwan.
The war in Iran has also been a sticking point, with Beijing the largest buyer of Tehran's oil and its largest trade partner.

Chinese state media reported on Friday that Xi would take part in "bilateral" talks on the sidelines of the Apec summit, citing a foreign ministry spokesman, but has not reported on the trilateral meeting.
Earlier this month, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Russian state media that there were "signals confirming readiness" for such talks at the summit.
Xi basks in spotlight as he hosts Putin days after Trump
body_zh: 白宫表示，唐纳德·特朗普、弗拉基米尔·普京和习近平计划在下周中国峰会期间会面。
发言人奥利维亚·威尔士对记者表示，美国、俄罗斯和中国领导人之间的历史性会晤将在特朗普出席在南部城市深圳举行的亚太经济合作组织（APEC）峰会期间举行。
“总统已明确表示，除其他议题外，他将讨论世界范围内核武器的削减，特朗普总统认为核武器的扩散非常危险，”她说。
据了解，世界最大核大国会议期间也可能讨论伊朗问题，但不会讨论乌克兰问题。俄罗斯已确认此次会面。中国尚未做出反应。
据美联社和路透社报道，一位不愿透露姓名的美国高级官员表示，预计会谈后不会达成协议。
特朗普将于周三晚些时候抵达深圳，参加为期两天的21个成员国峰会。他还将参加周四与习近平的双边会谈，这是自美国总统 2025 年重新就职以来他们的第四次会面。
威尔士说：“特朗普总统将通过美国总统、中华人民共和国主席和俄罗斯联邦总统之间的三方会晤来结束对中国的访问。”
她表示，特朗普此行还包括参加周二在菲律宾举行的东南亚国家联盟（东盟）峰会，这将“确保美国人民取得历史性胜利，并促进美国在印度太平洋地区的利益”。
美国和俄罗斯之间的核武器控制条约于二月到期，导致世界上最大的核武库失去了重要的护栏，并有效地标志着有助于解决冷战的军控合作的结束。
联合国敦促双方立即商定新框架。不过，特朗普表示，他可以用一项更好的协议来取代该协议，其中包括一直在增强核武库的中国。
美国前高级官员和分析人士当时告诉英国广播公司，寻求北京和莫斯科的合作可能会遇到重大障碍，并且需要数年时间。
今年早些时候，习近平在北京分别接待了普京和特朗普，时间相隔几天，而美国总统则于九月在华盛顿欢迎了中国总统。
自2022年全面入侵乌克兰以来，北京已成为莫斯科的重要贸易伙伴，这导致俄罗斯孤立并受到西方制裁。
但美国进口俄罗斯柴油的一项有争议的协议以及针对包括中国在内的莫斯科石油和天然气最大买家的制裁暂停，加剧了欧洲对特朗普政府上个月对克里姆林宫态度软化的担忧。
与此同时，特朗普和习近平试图在今年的北京和华盛顿峰会上展现更温暖的关系，尽管在贸易、人工智能主导地位之争和台湾等关键问题上似乎没有取得重大进展。
伊朗战争也是一个症结所在，北京是德黑兰石油的最大买家及其最大的贸易伙伴。
中国官方媒体周五援引外交部发言人的话说，习近平将在亚太经合组织峰会期间参加“双边”会谈，但尚未报道三边会议。
本月早些时候，克里姆林宫发言人德米特里·佩斯科夫对俄罗斯官方媒体表示，有“信号证实”峰会已准备好进行此类会谈。
